title: feat(pm): card-pick reader, os-verify-lock --depth and check-prior-rulings --paths replace three retyped procedures
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-bill"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wgXFRsfSS1tQB1kBxAZ86579)_

Part of #35237
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化:产品用户看不到变化;车队席位从此一条命令就能拿到"下一张该取哪张卡"的排序清单,连同其余每张卡为什么不能取;派发前查排队深度、查旧裁决和前提是否过时,也各自变成一条命令。
- 为什么做:这几步过去每轮都由席位照着规则文字手工重做,容易漏读、取错卡;交给脚本后规则只算一遍,规则文字一改,脚本自检就会报红。
- 出错会怎样:三个脚本只读不写,出错最多是给席位一个错误的排序或读数,认领前的复读仍然把关;读不全时它们明说"不完整",不会给出看似干净的结果;旧裁决是否被引用由席位逐行读,脚本只列出要读的行。
- 要你做什么:无,席位按审核记录落地。

## What changes

This is slice 1 of the card: three readers replace three procedures that the dispatch rules spell as prose and that every executing seat retypes. Each prose passage shrinks to a pointer naming the command.

- **`scripts/pm/card-pick.mjs` (new).** Read-only. It lists every open `pm:queue` issue (every page, the count checked against the platform's search total), reads each named epic's sub-issue order, and ranks the cards by `docs/NORTH-STAR.md` "Priority" rule 3: p0, then p1 from any area, then the `--order` items in turn (an epic by its child order whatever the grade; an area by its p2 cards, then its p3 cards under the leg `order k p3 close-out`), then the ungraded leg. An area's p3 ranks after every p2 of that item and before the next item, so an area holding only p3 cards yields its p3 as the next pick. At one grade it orders a non-fleet card first, then a Bug, then the oldest card. A card is not a pick when it has an assignee, `pm:dispatched`, `needs-user-decision`, `pm:retriage`, a second pm state, an epic or tracking parent, an open line-start `Blocked-by:` target in the body or a comment (a PR target holds until it merges), a newest `Claim:` with no `Release:` after it, or (a fleet card) no triage audit record. Every row prints the card's `domain:*` labels. `--why` prints every other queue card with its named blocking point. Threads are read lazily in rank order, all of them with `--why`. The footer always names the seven legs it cannot read: the maintainer's direct dispatch, the contract-surface leg, a `tooling` card's three-gate admission, the multi-seat alternation, batching a p3 onto a PR, lane ownership (a `domain:*` card outside the seat's lane, a cloud card or a security card is listed but may not be claimed) and an area item that holds a sub-epic (rule 3 ③ binds that sub-epic's child order; name it as `epic:#N` to get it). Flags: `--repo --order --seat --limit --why --json --fixture --now --self-test`; `--order` with no value is a usage error, `--order ""` is the p0/p1-only order; `--seat` parses by the seat signature's own grammar, so an epic seat's `epic:#N#1` is accepted. Exits: 0 complete, 2 usage, 3 queue unreadable, 4 incomplete. A thread, a `Blocked-by:` target or a sub-issue parent that cannot be read makes the run incomplete with the gap named, and every card such a read holds is printed even without `--why`.
  - Reused, not re-spelled: from `check-half-states.mjs` `blockerTargetsFor` (which wraps `blockedByTargets` and `commentBlockedByTargets`), `blockerResolutionFromRow`, `isFleetCard`, `readSignatureLine` and `SEAT_SIGNATURE_LINE`, `markerMatches` with the claim and release markers, `gradeRung` / `GRADE_LADDER`, `h67ReadOrder` (the same-grade age order; a stable sort adds the Bug tiebreak above age) and H74's triage-audit reader with its parent read. From `gh-pages.mjs`: `readAllPages`, `ghApi`.
- **`scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh --depth`.** A read-only mode next to `--status`. It prints `depth D (queue Q + 1) · hold at 2 → go|wait`, without counting the holder, parked slots or dead tickets. It counts WITHOUT pruning: it judges each ticket with the same `ticket_state` and leaves a dead ticket in place, naming it, so the next `--status` still prints that ticket's liveness verdict (`queue_live` would delete it, and `--depth` runs before every dispatch). On a host with no usable `flock` it discloses DECLARED UNLOCKED MODE as `--status` does. It exits 0 for go, 1 for wait and 3 when the liveness probe is unlit or the host cannot operate the lock (never read as depth 1). `LOCK_DEPTH_HOLD=2` now lives in the script.
- **`scripts/pm/check-prior-rulings.mjs --paths`.** The pre-dispatch premise readings over a declared file surface.
  - ① greps the four ruling words the rule names (`ruling`, `Ruling-ref`, `maintainer`, `⛔`), fixed-string, at the revision, and prints a per-word count with `file:line`. Whether a hit cites a ruling is a reading of the hit, so the reader does not classify it: per file it prints the reading owed, 「逐行读:引裁决 ⇒ id+原句入裁决区;不引 ⇒ 计数」, and never a count outcome. An id-shape match (`ADR-NNN` or a record id) is tagged on its line as a hint only, because a ruling is as often cited by name, date or card number (`ruling A′, 2026-09-13`, `ruling A+, #31491`). The one verdict it prints is 「零命中 → 无裁决」, and only when every declared path matched a file at the revision: a path that matched none is named and the clean verdict is withheld. When a word's hits pass the per-word cap, the rest are counted and the exact `git grep` that lists them is printed.
  - ② runs `git log -20` on the paths. When one of those commits is dated today (UTC), it prints `dispatch-runbook.md`'s same-day line verbatim.
  - ③ reads the `#N` and `owner/repo#N` refs the card body and its thread name, scoped to the swept repository: a ref in it is read for its state, merge, assignees and title; a ref in another repository of the same owner for open or closed and assignees only; a ref outside that owner is listed by number and not fetched; an `owner/repo` that is not two plain names (a dot-only segment, for one) is rejected and not fetched. It needs `--card`; without it the face says `not read`.
  - ④ names the faces it does not read under every run: the work-item face, GitHub URLs in the card or thread (listed by number) and cards named on ruling-hit lines (listed by number, not followed).
  - `--paths` alone skips the term search.
- **`package.json`:** `check:pm-prior-rulings` now also runs `card-pick.mjs --self-test`. This adds no CI job: the existing "Prior-ruling reader self-test" step runs the chain.
- **Prose, no ratchet ceiling touched:**
  - `execution-duties.md` (189 → 184): the ruling-area grep, the action face and the card-ref face become one pointer to `check-prior-rulings.mjs --paths`. The two depth lines become one pointer to `--depth`. The pick-order lines become one line that defines 标签序 as NORTH-STAR rule 3 with its last leg 无级, scoped to the lane's open cards, and points at `card-pick.mjs --order ORDER`. Kept as written: the candidate definition (「开放 = 未派发(无 `pm:dispatched`、无 assignee);在飞的 P0/P1 不挡任何候选,只余取卡全序。」), 取卡全序 with its three legs, the work-item face line, the cloud lane, the per-level reading, the same-grade line and the alternation line.
  - `seat-lifecycle.md` (99 → 98): the three queue-empty lines become two: the pointer to `card-pick.mjs --order ORDER --why` with 「无卡点即候选,⛔ 不得报空」, and the one blocking-point vocabulary, now with `outside --order`.
  - `coordinator.md` (51 → 51): the pick surface points at `card-pick.mjs --order ORDER`. The batch line keeps its rule sentence 「p0/p1 先,余照点名次序」 and names `card-pick.mjs` as its reading for queue cards; a PR row, a resumed card or a claimed card still takes the sentence. 「满即排队」 joins the free-slot line and 「交回或合入即释放槽位」 the slot-accounting line, so no line grows past 120 bytes.

## Live run

Two runs against the board at head `1bdac164b5`. The first is the command as the pointer names it: `node scripts/pm/card-pick.mjs --order area:fleet --seat repo:objectstack#5 --why`, exit 0, 292 lines, trimmed:

## Tests

- `node scripts/pm/card-pick.mjs --self-test`: `✓ card-pick self-test: 62 cases pass across 8 batteries — offline, no network.` The batteries are pinned by name with a floor, plus the handshake. They pin: p0 above everything; an unnamed-area p1 beating a named-area p2; an area holding only p3 cards yielding p3 picks, a p2 always ranking ahead of a p3 in the same item, an item's p3 closing that item before the next item's p2, a p3 outside the order not picked, and an epic's children following child order whatever the grade; an open target blocking, a closed-unmerged PR target still blocking, a merged PR and a closed issue releasing, a comment-borne line holding, a cross-repo target read from its own repo; the same-grade tiebreaks; epic child order; the claim, release and triage-audit readings; paging, the count gap, `--limit` and `--why`; an unreadable thread, `Blocked-by:` target or sub-issue parent making the run incomplete with the gap named and the held card printed without `--why`; the CLI exits, `--order` with no value, `--seat` with an epic lane, the `domain:*` on the row and the seven-leg footer. The drift pin quotes NORTH-STAR rule 3's four clauses and asserts each present, alongside the execution-duties phrases, the state-machine phrases and the seat-lifecycle phrases (the pointer with `--order`, the vocabulary with `outside --order`).
- `bash scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh --self-test`: `✓ os-verify-lock self-test: all cases pass.` Eight `--depth` cases: an empty queue reads depth 1 and goes; a host with no usable `flock` discloses DECLARED UNLOCKED MODE; the holder and a parked slot are not counted; a live waiter reaches depth 2 and exits 1; a dead ticket is not counted, is named, and is still on disk after the run; the next `--status` prints that ticket's liveness verdict; an unlit probe exits 3 and prints no depth; `LOCK_DEPTH_HOLD` equals the value the rule line names.
- `node scripts/pm/check-prior-rulings.mjs --self-test`: `✓ check-prior-rulings self-test: 185 cases pass`. 30 of them are `--paths` cases (18 before this round). They pin: on a fixture shaped like the rule's worked example (`screen-input-contract.ts`, hits citing `ruling A′, 2026-09-13` and `ruling A+, #31491`), every hit is listed for reading under the reading owed and gets no count verdict and no 无裁决; an id shape is a hint, the same reading owed; a declared path that matched no file withholds the clean verdict and is named; past the per-word cap the rest are counted with the exact `git grep`; a ref outside the swept repository's owner is not fetched and is listed by number; a `../x#1` ref is rejected and not fetched; a same-owner ref prints open or closed and assignees, no title; same-day is the commit's UTC day, so a commit whose offset date is a different calendar day from its UTC date is judged by the UTC day; the log is `-20` at the revision on the declared glob pathspecs; the unread faces with their URL and ruling-hit refs; and the drift pins on execution-duties and on dispatch-runbook's same-day line.

## Acceptance notes

- **Where the scoping note and `main` differ, `main` was encoded.** (a) The scoping note lists "no triage audit" as a blocking point. `seat-lifecycle.md`'s vocabulary on main says the same, so it excludes the card; it uses H74's reader, parent exemption included. (b) Main's label order ends with the ungraded leg, which the note did not list; it is encoded after every graded order item, and `execution-duties.md` names it (无级殿后). (c) Main says p3 is "left for the close-out or batched" and, in an area with no sub-epic, "p2 before p3". So an area's p3 cards are picks, ranked after every p2 of that item (leg `order k p3 close-out`). The reader cannot tell whether an area holds a sub-epic, so every area item ranks this way and the footer names that leg; a sub-epic named as an `epic:` item keeps its child order. Batching a p3 onto a PR is a judgement over a diff, so the footer names it as a leg the reader does not judge. (d) `tooling`'s three-gate admission is triage's reading; only one gate is a machine line. The row is flagged and the footer names the gap; nothing is excluded on it.
- **Lane ownership is printed, not judged.** The reader lists the whole `pm:queue` board; a `domain:*` seat's candidate set is its lane, and a `repo:objectstack` seat does not claim a cloud card or a security card. The row's `domain:*` and the footer leg carry that to the seat; `execution-duties.md` scopes 标签序 to the lane's open cards.
- **Not taken in this round:** 「裁决同罪」 (the old staleness line's "rulings too") has no successor line; the `--paths` pointer line has no room under 120 bytes, and the ruling-area step it names already covers rulings. The work-item face keeps its own line in `execution-duties.md` unchanged, and the reader now names it under every run as a face it does not read.
- **The optional `lanes/director.md` rider was not taken.** That line re-runs the grep "逐仓" (per repo), and `check-prior-rulings.mjs` reads its tree corpora from this checkout only. A pointer would change the rule for cards in other repos, which this PR is not deciding.
- **Remaining slices of the card** (separate PRs, `Part of`): landing reads (`landing-k`, `pr-state`, `sweep-closed-cards --pr`); the round health line (after #35373); in-flight status and round-open (after #35232 / #35235); the deferred `area-lease.md` and `dispatch-runbook.md` pointers; `l1-face`; the os-dev pointers (`git-history ancestor`, `dev-worktree`, after #35231).
